\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

Machine learning has achieved remarkable results in recent years.
Deep neural networks~\cite{lecun2015deep} have become the dominant
paradigm for supervised learning tasks.  In this work we study the
convergence properties of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) applied
to non-convex loss surfaces.

The main contributions are:
\begin{itemize}
\item A new bound on the expected loss after $T$ iterations.
\item Empirical validation on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.
\item An open-source implementation in PyTorch.
\end{itemize}

\section{Background}
\label{sec:background}

Let $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable loss function.
SGD updates the parameter vector $\theta_t$ at step $t$ via:
\[
\theta_{t+1} = \theta_t - \eta_t \nabla f(\theta_t; \xi_t)
\]
where $\eta_t > 0$ is the learning rate and $\xi_t$ is a mini-batch
sampled uniformly from the training set.

We assume the following standard conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Lipschitz gradients:} $\|\nabla f(x) - \nabla f(y)\| \leq L\|x - y\|$ for all $x, y$.
\item \textbf{Bounded variance:} $\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(\theta; \xi) - \nabla f(\theta)\|^2] \leq \sigma^2$.
\item \textbf{Lower-bounded loss:} $f(\theta) \geq f^*$ for all $\theta$.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Main Result}
\label{sec:main}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:convergence}
Under conditions (1)--(3), SGD with step size $\eta_t = \eta / \sqrt{T}$ satisfies:
\[
\frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(\theta_t)\|^2]
\leq \frac{2(f(\theta_0) - f^*)}{\eta \sqrt{T}} + \frac{L \eta \sigma^2}{\sqrt{T}}
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By the $L$-smoothness assumption we have $f(\theta_{t+1}) \leq f(\theta_t)
+ \langle \nabla f(\theta_t), \theta_{t+1} - \theta_t \rangle
+ \frac{L}{2}\|\theta_{t+1} - \theta_t\|^2$.  Substituting the SGD update
and taking expectations yields the result after telescoping.
\end{proof}

See Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} and Section~\ref{sec:background} for details.

\section{Conclusion}

We proved a $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ convergence rate for SGD on smooth non-convex
objectives.  Future work includes extending to Adam~\cite{kingma2014adam}
and investigating the effect of momentum.
